It is my distinct honor and pleasure to welcome the representatives of Virginia's world-class university technology transfer offices here today. These university workers are engines of innovation. The men and women who staff our technology transfer offices serve as a vital bridge between the laboratory and the marketplace, protecting discoveries, forging partnerships with industry and ensuring that the public investments made in research yield lasting

public benefit. Here's some statewide statistics that they have contributed to. We have had 115 technologies that were successfully licensed for commercial applications, 27 new licenses granted to new technology startups, the majority located right here in Virginia, creating jobs and companies in our own backyard. A couple of examples from VCU researchers. Someone has developed a vaccine for Lyme disease that is licensed for veterinary care currently and is in phase three

Researchers at UVA have received FDA approval for a groundbreaking treatment of acute myeloid leukemia, one of the most aggressive and deadly blood cancers known to

medicine. The research was done in partnership with the University of Michigan and Cura Oncology, who has licensed the IP. In another landmark achievement, a major medical device company has licensed a specific controlled algorithm for insulin pumps. And then last but not least are Virginia Tech's researchers, who were recently featured by Time Magazine as an example of transformative medical technology in the nano knife system.

It's a non-thermal technique that ablates soft tissue, including tumors with remarkable precision, and will lead the way in cancer research. The discoveries described here represent only a fraction of the innovation emerging from Virginia's universities each year.

The General Assembly supports these amazing technology transfer offices, and this means that more companies are formed, more jobs are created, more patents are protected, and more lives are improved. They are making Virginia more competitive, more prosperous, and more resilient.
